    Extract resolved computation settings from a result

    Source: R/settings.R
    mssr_settings.Rd

    Validates a result and returns arguments that can be passed to mssr() with the retained original input. The grid is included explicitly; derived kernel sizes and resource limits are not computation settings returned here.

    Usage

    mssr_settings(result)

    Arguments

    result

    A result returned by mssr(), mssr_temporal() or mssr_read_result().

    Value

    A named list containing fwhm, amp, order, intensity_normalize, mesh, grid, kernel and rounding. For a temporal result it also starts with statistic and frames (the frame indices of the original input), plus sign for the SOFI statistics, so that it can be passed to mssr_temporal() together with the original raw frames (not with an mssr_stack, which refuses per-frame settings).

    Details

    These are resolved settings, not the original call. For example, mesh is FALSE when amplification is 1 because it had no effect. Records from a different numerical engine are refused: this helper does not migrate historical engines. A legacy result schema is accepted when its engine matches and its stored contract validates.

    Retain the original input, preprocessing and channel/frame selection, acquisition information, and mask region, fraction and seed separately. Result files do not contain them. Set resource budgets explicitly when recomputing. Preserve the package and runtime environment, check engine identity, and compare recomputed values; matching settings alone do not guarantee identical arithmetic across environments or versions. This function needs no optional packages and does not modify the result.

    Examples

    x <- matrix(seq_len(35), 5, 7)
result <- mssr(x, fwhm = 2.5, amp = 2, grid = "endpoint")
replay <- do.call(mssr, c(list(x = x, max_memory_bytes = 1024^3),
                          mssr_settings(result)))
identical(replay$values, result$values)
#> [1] TRUE
